28# The ATen schema names the keyword arg ``range``, which shadows the builtin. 

29# Grab the builtin here so host-side loops still work inside the implementation. 

30import builtins as _builtins # noqa: E402 

31 

32# GCU400 has 24 SIPs; at most 48 CTAs run concurrently, so grids above that 

33# only add wave-quantisation and per-program setup cost. 

34NUM_SIPS = 24 

35MAX_CTAS = NUM_SIPS * 2 

36 

37# Host-side metadata caches. ``torch.tensor`` copies to the device cost ~30 us 

38# each on pageable transfers, and the per-call host path used to pay four of 

39# them (lefts / rights / strides / bins) plus an edges kernel launch on every 

40# invocation. The metadata depends only on (device, bins, range), so it is 

41# built once and reused; repeated calls with the same configuration -- the 

42# dominant pattern in serving loops and benchmarks -- skip the transfers 

43# entirely. Entries are small (a few hundred floats); the cap keeps a caller 

44# sweeping many distinct ranges from growing the cache without bound. 

45_META_CACHE_CAP = 64 

46_BINS_META_CACHE = {} 

47_RANGE_META_CACHE = {} 

48_PARTIALS_CACHE = {} 

49 

50# Above this size a weighted call falls back from the per-program private 

51# slab (one row of ``num_bins`` per program) to direct atomics, so a huge 

52# point cloud over a wide bin grid cannot force a multi-GB scratch tensor. 

53_MAX_SLAB_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024 

54 

55# Dispatch thresholds, measured on GCU400 with the bench shapes 

56# (see the module history / case log for the probe data): 

57# * one-hot int8 ``tl.dot`` beats ``tl.histogram`` for small bin counts 

58# (the histogram primitive pays ~69 ns per bin per program, so E=512 

59# costs ~100 us per program while the dot's per-point cost grows only 

60# with the bin count); 

61# * for wide bin vectors the per-point one-hot compare cost overtakes it 

62# and ``tl.histogram`` + a partial-store wins again; 

63# * per-program atomics serialize at ~100 ns per lane on GCU400, so 

64# histogram combination always goes through per-program partials plus 

65# a single reduce kernel instead of same-address global atomics. 

66_DOT_PERSISTENT_MAX_BINS = 128 # HIST_BINS <= this: single-chunk persistent dot 

67_DOT_MAX_POINTS = 32768 # M below this: chunked dot, else tl.histogram 

68_HIST_BLOCK = 2048 # BLOCK_SIZE for the tl.histogram path 

69_DOT_BLOCK = 512 

70_SLAB_BLOCK = 512 

71 

72 

73def _meta_cache_put(cache, key, value): 

74 if len(cache) >= _META_CACHE_CAP: 

75 cache.clear() 

76 cache[key] = value 

77 return value

80@triton.jit 

81def _histdd_locate( 

82 inp_ptr, 

83 row_start, 

84 row_mask, 

85 M, 

86 N, 

87 left_ptr, 

88 right_ptr, 

89 edges_ptr, 

90 strides_ptr, 

91 bins_ptr, 

92 MAX_EDGES, 

93 MAX_EDGE_STEPS: tl.constexpr, 

94 N_CONST: tl.constexpr, 

95 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

96): 

97 """Locate each row's flat bin index, or mark the row invalid. 

98 

99 Shared prologue of every counting kernel: walks the dimensions, range- 

100 checks the coordinate and binary-searches the explicit edge array that 

101 ATen builds with linspace. Returns (linear_idx, valid); the caller routes 

102 invalid lanes wherever its counting strategy prefers (padding bin, or a 

103 masked-off atomic). 

104 """ 

105 valid = row_mask 

106 # num_bins is bounded by the product of the small per-dimension bin 

107 # counts, so a 32-bit linear index is sufficient and avoids GCU's slow 

108 # int64 path. 

109 linear_idx = tl.zeros((BLOCK_SIZE,), dtype=tl.int32) 

110 

111 for d in range(N_CONST): 

112 coord = tl.load( 

113 inp_ptr + row_start * N_CONST + d, mask=row_mask, other=float("nan") 

114 ).to(tl.float32) 

115 left = tl.load(left_ptr + d).to(tl.float32) 

116 right = tl.load(right_ptr + d).to(tl.float32) 

117 nbins = tl.load(bins_ptr + d) 

118 stride = tl.load(strides_ptr + d) 

119 

120 # Only count points inside [left, right] (NaN fails both comparisons). 

121 in_range = (coord >= left) & (coord <= right) 

122 valid = valid & in_range 

123 

124 # Locate the bin by searching the explicit edge array, which is what 

125 # ATen does -- it materialises the edges with linspace and takes an 

126 # upper bound over them. No closed-form index reproduces that: 

127 # computing floor((coord - left) * bins / width) puts 0.3 over 

128 # [0, 1] with 10 bins in bin 3 where ATen says 2, and 

129 # floor((coord - left) / bin_width) fixes 0.3 but then misplaces 

130 # 0.6 and 0.7. Searching the same edges the native op builds agrees 

131 # on every probed value. 

132 row = edges_ptr + d * MAX_EDGES 

133 lo = tl.zeros((BLOCK_SIZE,), dtype=tl.int32) 

134 hi = tl.full((BLOCK_SIZE,), 0, dtype=tl.int32) + nbins 

135 # Binary search for the last edge <= coord, over at most 

136 # log2(MAX_EDGES) steps; the trip count is a compile-time bound so 

137 # the loop unrolls. 

138 for _ in range(MAX_EDGE_STEPS): 

139 mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2 

140 mid_c = tl.minimum(mid, nbins) 

141 edge = tl.load(row + mid_c, mask=valid, other=float("inf")).to(tl.float32) 

142 take = (edge <= coord) & (mid <= nbins) 

143 lo = tl.where(take, mid, lo) 

144 hi = tl.where(take, hi, mid - 1) 

145 bin_idx = lo 

146 

147 # The rightmost bin is inclusive of its right edge, so a point 

148 # exactly on `right` searches to index nbins and must fold back 

149 # into the last bin. 

150 bin_idx = tl.where(bin_idx >= nbins, nbins - 1, bin_idx) 

151 bin_idx = tl.where(bin_idx < 0, 0, bin_idx) 

152 

153 linear_idx = linear_idx + bin_idx * stride 

154 

155 return linear_idx, valid 

156

158@libentry() 

159@triton.jit 

160def histogramdd_dot_persistent_kernel( 

161 inp_ptr, # (M, N) contiguous float32 input 

162 part_ptr, # (grid, HIST_BINS) int32 per-program partial counts 

163 M, 

164 N, 

165 left_ptr, # (N,) left edges 

166 right_ptr, # (N,) right edges 

167 edges_ptr, # (N, MAX_EDGES) per-dimension bin edges, row-padded 

168 strides_ptr, # (N,) row-major strides in bins 

169 bins_ptr, # (N,) number of bins per dim 

170 MAX_EDGES, 

171 MAX_EDGE_STEPS: tl.constexpr, 

172 N_CONST: tl.constexpr, 

173 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

174 NUM_BINS: tl.constexpr, 

175 HIST_BINS: tl.constexpr, 

176 NB_CHUNK: tl.constexpr, 

177): 

178 """Count points with a one-hot int8 ``tl.dot`` on a persistent grid. 

179 

180 ``count[b] = sum_e (key_e == b)`` lowers to 

181 ``ones[16, BLOCK] @ onehot[BLOCK, NBINS]`` on the MMA path, which is far 

182 cheaper than the serial ``tl.histogram`` update for narrow bin vectors. 

183 The grid is capped at the number of resident CTAs and each program 

184 strides over point blocks, accumulating its partial histogram across 

185 iterations; one partial row per program is then summed by the reduce 

186 kernel. No global atomics are issued at all. 

187 """ 

188 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

189 num_pids = tl.num_programs(0) 

190 ones = tl.full((16, BLOCK_SIZE), 1, dtype=tl.int8) 

191 acc = tl.zeros((16, NB_CHUNK), dtype=tl.int32) 

192 nblocks = tl.cdiv(M, BLOCK_SIZE) 

193 for blk in tl.range(pid, nblocks, num_pids): 

194 row_start = blk * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

195 row_mask = row_start < M 

196 linear_idx, valid = _histdd_locate( 

197 inp_ptr, 

198 row_start, 

199 row_mask, 

200 M, 

201 N, 

202 left_ptr, 

203 right_ptr, 

204 edges_ptr, 

205 strides_ptr, 

206 bins_ptr, 

207 MAX_EDGES, 

208 MAX_EDGE_STEPS, 

209 N_CONST, 

210 BLOCK_SIZE, 

211 ) 

212 # Invalid lanes are routed into the padding bin and dropped by the 

213 # store mask below (tl.histogram's mask is ignored by the GCU 

214 # backend; the same convention keeps the dot path uniform). 

215 key = tl.where(valid, linear_idx, HIST_BINS - 1) 

216 cols = tl.arange(0, NB_CHUNK) 

217 onehot = tl.where( 

218 key[:, None] == cols[None, :], 

219 tl.full((BLOCK_SIZE, NB_CHUNK), 1, tl.int8), 

220 tl.zeros((BLOCK_SIZE, NB_CHUNK), dtype=tl.int8), 

221 ) 

222 acc = tl.dot(ones, onehot, acc, out_dtype=tl.int32) 

223 # All 16 rows of `ones` are identical, so any row of `acc` holds the 

224 # counts; `tl.max` extracts one of them as a flat vector. 

225 counts = tl.max(acc, axis=0) 

226 out_cols = tl.arange(0, NB_CHUNK) 

227 tl.store(part_ptr + pid * HIST_BINS + out_cols, counts, mask=out_cols < HIST_BINS) 

228

230@libentry() 

231@triton.jit 

232def histogramdd_dot_kernel( 

233 inp_ptr, # (M, N) contiguous float32 input 

234 part_ptr, # (grid, HIST_BINS) int32 per-program partial counts 

235 M, 

236 N, 

237 left_ptr, # (N,) left edges 

238 right_ptr, # (N,) right edges 

239 edges_ptr, # (N, MAX_EDGES) per-dimension bin edges, row-padded 

240 strides_ptr, # (N,) row-major strides in bins 

241 bins_ptr, # (N,) number of bins per dim 

242 MAX_EDGES, 

243 MAX_EDGE_STEPS: tl.constexpr, 

244 N_CONST: tl.constexpr, 

245 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

246 NUM_BINS: tl.constexpr, 

247 HIST_BINS: tl.constexpr, 

248 NB_CHUNK: tl.constexpr, 

249): 

250 """Chunked one-hot int8 ``tl.dot`` counting, one program per point tile. 

251 

252 Used when the padded bin vector is wider than the single-chunk DSM 

253 budget (BLOCK x CHUNK int8 <= 64 KB); the bin axis is swept in NB_CHUNK 

254 chunks, each producing its own ``tl.dot``. Partials are stored per 

255 program and reduced by ``histogramdd_reduce_i32_kernel``. 

256 """ 

257 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

258 row_start = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

259 row_mask = row_start < M 

260 linear_idx, valid = _histdd_locate( 

261 inp_ptr, 

262 row_start, 

263 row_mask, 

264 M, 

265 N, 

266 left_ptr, 

267 right_ptr, 

268 edges_ptr, 

269 strides_ptr, 

270 bins_ptr, 

271 MAX_EDGES, 

272 MAX_EDGE_STEPS, 

273 N_CONST, 

274 BLOCK_SIZE, 

275 ) 

276 key = tl.where(valid, linear_idx, HIST_BINS - 1) 

277 ones = tl.full((16, BLOCK_SIZE), 1, dtype=tl.int8) 

278 for cbase in tl.static_range(0, HIST_BINS, NB_CHUNK): 

279 cols = cbase + tl.arange(0, NB_CHUNK) 

280 onehot = tl.where( 

281 key[:, None] == cols[None, :], 

282 tl.full((BLOCK_SIZE, NB_CHUNK), 1, tl.int8), 

283 tl.zeros((BLOCK_SIZE, NB_CHUNK), dtype=tl.int8), 

284 ) 

285 acc = tl.dot(ones, onehot, out_dtype=tl.int32) 

286 counts = tl.max(acc, axis=0) 

287 tl.store(part_ptr + pid * HIST_BINS + cols, counts, mask=cols < HIST_BINS)

290@libentry() 

291@triton.jit 

292def histogramdd_hist_partial_kernel( 

293 inp_ptr, # (M, N) contiguous float32 input 

294 part_ptr, # (grid, HIST_BINS) int32 per-program partial counts 

295 M, 

296 N, 

297 left_ptr, # (N,) left edges 

298 right_ptr, # (N,) right edges 

299 edges_ptr, # (N, MAX_EDGES) per-dimension bin edges, row-padded 

300 strides_ptr, # (N,) row-major strides in bins 

301 bins_ptr, # (N,) number of bins per dim 

302 MAX_EDGES, 

303 MAX_EDGE_STEPS: tl.constexpr, 

304 N_CONST: tl.constexpr, 

305 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

306 HIST_BINS: tl.constexpr, 

307): 

308 """``tl.histogram`` per program, storing a private partial row. 

309 

310 For wide bin vectors (HIST_BINS > 128) the per-point one-hot compare cost 

311 of the dot path overtakes the histogram primitive's per-bin cost, and 

312 ``tl.histogram`` wins again. Each program counts its tile into a private 

313 partial row -- no global atomics, no zero-initialised accumulator; the 

314 reduce kernel sums the rows into the output. 

315 """ 

316 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

317 row_start = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

318 row_mask = row_start < M 

319 linear_idx, valid = _histdd_locate( 

320 inp_ptr, 

321 row_start, 

322 row_mask, 

323 M, 

324 N, 

325 left_ptr, 

326 right_ptr, 

327 edges_ptr, 

328 strides_ptr, 

329 bins_ptr, 

330 MAX_EDGES, 

331 MAX_EDGE_STEPS, 

332 N_CONST, 

333 BLOCK_SIZE, 

334 ) 

335 # tl.histogram's mask is ignored by the GCU backend, so invalid lanes are 

336 # routed into the last (padding) bin and dropped by the store mask. 

337 hist_input = tl.where(valid, linear_idx, HIST_BINS - 1) 

338 local_counts = tl.histogram(hist_input, HIST_BINS) 

339 bin_offsets = tl.arange(0, HIST_BINS) 

340 tl.store( 

341 part_ptr + pid * HIST_BINS + bin_offsets, 

342 local_counts, 

343 mask=bin_offsets < HIST_BINS, 

344 )

347@libentry() 

348@triton.jit 

349def histogramdd_direct_kernel( 

350 inp_ptr, # (M, N) contiguous float32 input 

351 weight_ptr, # (M,) contiguous weights, or a dummy when HAS_WEIGHT=False 

352 out_ptr, # (num_bins,) zero-initialised accumulator 

353 M, 

354 N, 

355 left_ptr, # (N,) left edges 

356 right_ptr, # (N,) right edges 

357 edges_ptr, # (N, MAX_EDGES) per-dimension bin edges, row-padded 

358 strides_ptr, # (N,) row-major strides in bins 

359 bins_ptr, # (N,) number of bins per dim 

360 MAX_EDGES, 

361 MAX_EDGE_STEPS: tl.constexpr, 

362 N_CONST: tl.constexpr, 

363 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

364 HAS_WEIGHT: tl.constexpr, 

365): 

366 """Per-point atomic accumulation into one shared histogram buffer. 

367 

368 Kept for bin grids too wide for any per-program aggregation to pay off 

369 (the per-point one-hot / histogram cost grows with the bin count while 

370 the atomic cost does not), and as the fallback for pathological weighted 

371 calls whose private slab would exceed the scratch budget. The buffer 

372 must be zeroed before launch; combination across programs happens 

373 through same-address atomics, which is fine here because wide bin grids 

374 keep the per-address collision count low. 

375 """ 

376 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

377 row_start = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

378 row_mask = row_start < M 

379 linear_idx, valid = _histdd_locate( 

380 inp_ptr, 

381 row_start, 

382 row_mask, 

383 M, 

384 N, 

385 left_ptr, 

386 right_ptr, 

387 edges_ptr, 

388 strides_ptr, 

389 bins_ptr, 

390 MAX_EDGES, 

391 MAX_EDGE_STEPS, 

392 N_CONST, 

393 BLOCK_SIZE, 

394 ) 

395 if HAS_WEIGHT: 

396 contrib = tl.load(weight_ptr + row_start, mask=valid, other=0.0).to(tl.float32) 

397 else: 

398 contrib = tl.full((BLOCK_SIZE,), 1.0, dtype=tl.float32) 

399 tl.atomic_add(out_ptr + linear_idx, contrib, mask=valid, sem="relaxed") 

400

402@libentry() 

403@triton.jit 

404def histogramdd_weighted_slab_kernel( 

405 inp_ptr, # (M, N) contiguous float32 input 

406 weight_ptr, # (M,) contiguous float32 weights 

407 slab_ptr, # (grid, NUM_BINS) zero-initialised private rows 

408 M, 

409 N, 

410 left_ptr, # (N,) left edges 

411 right_ptr, # (N,) right edges 

412 edges_ptr, # (N, MAX_EDGES) per-dimension bin edges, row-padded 

413 strides_ptr, # (N,) row-major strides in bins 

414 bins_ptr, # (N,) number of bins per dim 

415 MAX_EDGES, 

416 MAX_EDGE_STEPS: tl.constexpr, 

417 N_CONST: tl.constexpr, 

418 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

419 NUM_BINS: tl.constexpr, 

420): 

421 """Weighted accumulation into per-program private slab rows. 

422 

423 Weights break every counting primitive (``tl.histogram`` counts 

424 occurrences, the one-hot dot counts too), so a weighted histogram has to 

425 scatter-add one contribution per point. Doing that into one shared 

426 buffer serialises same-address atomics across all programs: for a 

427 million points over twenty bins that is a ~50 000-way collision per bin 

428 and measured 74 ms per call. Giving every program a private row caps the 

429 collision depth at the per-tile level; the reduce kernel then sums the 

430 rows. The slab is freshly zeroed per call. 

431 """ 

432 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

433 row_start = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

434 row_mask = row_start < M 

435 linear_idx, valid = _histdd_locate( 

436 inp_ptr, 

437 row_start, 

438 row_mask, 

439 M, 

440 N, 

441 left_ptr, 

442 right_ptr, 

443 edges_ptr, 

444 strides_ptr, 

445 bins_ptr, 

446 MAX_EDGES, 

447 MAX_EDGE_STEPS, 

448 N_CONST, 

449 BLOCK_SIZE, 

450 ) 

451 contrib = tl.load(weight_ptr + row_start, mask=valid, other=0.0).to(tl.float32) 

452 tl.atomic_add( 

453 slab_ptr + pid * NUM_BINS + linear_idx, contrib, mask=valid, sem="relaxed" 

454 ) 

455

457@libentry() 

458@triton.jit 

459def histogramdd_reduce_i32_kernel( 

460 part_ptr, # (n_prog, HIST_BINS) int32 partial counts 

461 out_ptr, # (num_bins,) float32 out; fully overwritten 

462 n_prog, 

463 HIST_BINS: tl.constexpr, 

464 NUM_BINS: tl.constexpr, 

465 BLOCK_B: tl.constexpr, 

466): 

467 """Sum per-program int32 partial rows into the float32 output. 

468 

469 Writes every bin (including untouched ones, as zeros), so the output 

470 needs no zero-initialisation and the reduce doubles as the full 

471 overwrite required by the ``.out`` contract. 

472 """ 

473 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

474 bins = pid * BLOCK_B + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_B) 

475 m = bins < NUM_BINS 

476 acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_B,), dtype=tl.int32) 

477 for p in range(0, n_prog): 

478 acc += tl.load(part_ptr + p * HIST_BINS + bins, mask=m, other=0) 

479 tl.store(out_ptr + bins, acc.to(tl.float32), mask=m) 

480

485 slab_ptr, # (n_prog, NUM_BINS) float32 private weighted rows

487 n_prog,

501@libentry() 

502@triton.jit 

503def histogramdd_density_kernel( 

504 hist_ptr, # (num_bins,) counts in ACC_DTYPE 

505 out_ptr, # (num_bins,) density output (input dtype) 

506 scale_ptr, # () scalar: 1 / (total_count * bin_volume) 

507 num_bins, 

508 ACC_DTYPE: tl.constexpr, 

509 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

510): 

511 """Normalize counts into a density: density[i] = count[i] / (total * volume).""" 

512 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

513 offset = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

514 mask = offset < num_bins 

515 count = tl.load(hist_ptr + offset, mask=mask, other=0.0) 

516 scale = tl.load(scale_ptr) 

517 # Stay in ACC_DTYPE so an fp64 histogram keeps full precision, and so a 

518 # non-finite scale (see the density notes in the host function) propagates 

519 # exactly as ATen's division does. 

520 density = count.to(ACC_DTYPE) * scale.to(ACC_DTYPE) 

521 tl.store(out_ptr + offset, density, mask=mask)

524@libentry() 

525@triton.jit 

526def histogramdd_col_range_kernel( 

527 inp_ptr, # (M, N) contiguous input 

528 left_ptr, # (N,) out: per-dimension left edge 

529 right_ptr, # (N,) out: per-dimension right edge 

530 nonfinite_ptr, # () out: lowest dimension with a non-finite value 

531 M, 

532 N, 

533 ACC_DTYPE: tl.constexpr, 

534 BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr, 

535 BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr, 

536 SENTINEL: tl.constexpr, 

537): 

538 """Per-column min/max, with the degenerate column widened to (min-.5, max+.5). 

539 

540 One program handles a tile of BLOCK_N columns and strides down the rows, so 

541 the whole auto-range computation happens on the device: this replaces host 

542 calls to ``torch.aminmax``/``torch.where``, which the FlagGems host-function 

543 convention does not allow. Results are written in ACC_DTYPE to keep fp64 

544 inputs exact. 

545 

546 The kernel also reports, into the single-element ``nonfinite_ptr``, the 

547 lowest dimension whose data contains a NaN or +-Inf. The host then only 

548 has to read that one scalar to decide whether to raise, instead of 

549 running ``isfinite`` / ``nonzero`` on the whole range tensor. 

550 """ 

551 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

552 cols = pid * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N) 

553 col_mask = cols < N 

554 

555 acc_min = tl.full((BLOCK_N,), float("inf"), dtype=ACC_DTYPE) 

556 acc_max = tl.full((BLOCK_N,), float("-inf"), dtype=ACC_DTYPE) 

557 # Whether each column has seen a NaN anywhere. Tracked separately from 

558 # the min/max accumulators so the NaN state is never carried through a 

559 # float reduction: ``tl.min``/``tl.max``/``tl.minimum``/``tl.maximum`` all 

560 # lower to fmin/fmax, which *ignore* a NaN operand, so a NaN folded into 

561 # the accumulator would simply be dropped by the identity +inf/-inf. 

562 nan_seen = tl.zeros((BLOCK_N,), dtype=tl.int1) 

563 # Whether each column has seen a NaN or +-Inf, i.e. whether its auto-range 

564 # cannot be finite. Separate from ``nan_seen`` because ATen's range check 

565 # rejects infinities too, which the min/max accumulators carry silently. 

566 nonfinite_seen = tl.zeros((BLOCK_N,), dtype=tl.int1) 

567 

568 for row_base in range(0, M, BLOCK_M): 

569 rows = row_base + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M) 

570 row_mask = rows < M 

571 vals = tl.load( 

572 inp_ptr + rows[:, None] * N + cols[None, :], 

573 mask=row_mask[:, None] & col_mask[None, :], 

574 other=float("nan"), 

575 ).to(ACC_DTYPE) 

576 # Masked-off lanes hold the NaN filler, so they are excluded 

577 # explicitly; they are not part of the data. 

578 live = row_mask[:, None] & col_mask[None, :] 

579 # Covariant with ``aminmax``: a column holding a NaN gets a NaN 

580 # range, not the min/max of the remaining values. 

581 nan_seen = nan_seen | (tl.sum((live & (vals != vals)).to(tl.int32), axis=0) > 0) 

582 nonfinite_seen = nonfinite_seen | ( 

583 tl.sum( 

584 (live & ((vals != vals) | (tl.abs(vals) == float("inf")))).to(tl.int32), 

585 axis=0, 

586 ) 

587 > 0 

588 ) 

589 acc_min = tl.minimum(acc_min, tl.min(vals, axis=0)) 

590 acc_max = tl.maximum(acc_max, tl.max(vals, axis=0)) 

591 

592 # A NaN column's range is NaN in both bounds; NaN == NaN is false, so the 

593 # degenerate-range expansion below leaves it alone, exactly as ATen does. 

594 acc_min = tl.where(nan_seen, float("nan"), acc_min) 

595 acc_max = tl.where(nan_seen, float("nan"), acc_max) 

596 

597 # A dimension whose min equals max is expanded, as torch.histogramdd does. 

598 same = acc_min == acc_max 

599 lefts = tl.where(same, acc_min - 0.5, acc_min) 

600 rights = tl.where(same, acc_max + 0.5, acc_max) 

601 tl.store(left_ptr + cols, lefts, mask=col_mask) 

602 tl.store(right_ptr + cols, rights, mask=col_mask) 

603 

604 # Publish the lowest offending dimension. ``tl.min`` within the tile plus 

605 # ``tl.atomic_min`` across programs reproduces ``(~finite).nonzero()[0]`` 

606 # without a host reduction. Lanes outside the tile (and every lane when 

607 # the column is finite) contribute the sentinel ``N``, which is above 

608 # every valid dimension, so a finite input leaves the host's ``N`` 

609 # untouched. 

610 cand = tl.min(tl.where(nonfinite_seen & col_mask, cols, SENTINEL), axis=0) 

611 tl.atomic_min(nonfinite_ptr, cand, sem="relaxed") 

612 

613 

614@libentry() 

615@triton.jit 

616def histogramdd_edges_kernel( 

617 left_ptr, # (N,) left edges 

618 right_ptr, # (N,) right edges 

619 bins_ptr, # (N,) bins per dimension 

620 edges_ptr, # (N, MAX_EDGES) out: padded per-dimension edge arrays 

621 N, 

622 MAX_EDGES, 

623 ACC_DTYPE: tl.constexpr, 

624 BLOCK_E: tl.constexpr, 

625): 

626 """Materialise the per-dimension bin edges the binning kernel searches. 

627 

628 Reproduces ``torch.linspace`` bit-for-bit, which is how ATen builds these 

629 edges. The precision matters more than usual here: a point sitting exactly 

630 on an edge is placed by an exact comparison, so a 1-ulp error in an edge 

631 moves that point a whole bin. Each rule below was settled by measuring 

632 against torch.linspace, with the mismatch counts over random 

633 configurations noted for the rejected variants. 

634 

635 * Interpolate from the nearer endpoint: ``step * i + left`` below the 

636 halfway index, ``right - step * (steps-1-i)`` at or above it. 

637 Accumulating from the left throughout puts edge 6 of [0, 1]/10 bins at 

638 0.6000000000000001 rather than 0.6, so a point at exactly 0.6 lands 

639 one bin low (113/300 disagree). 

640 * Derive ``step`` from endpoints already narrowed to the storage dtype. 

641 

642 GCU400 has no FP64 vector path: fp64 tensors are actually stored as fp32 

643 by torch_gcu and fp64 arithmetic crashes the GCU compiler. The whole 

644 linspace reproduction therefore stays in fp32 here, using ``div_rn`` for 

645 a correctly rounded step (plain fp32 `/` lowers to a fast reciprocal). 

646 """ 

647 d = ext.program_id(0) 

648 if d < N: 

649 left = tl.load(left_ptr + d) 

650 right = tl.load(right_ptr + d) 

651 nbins = tl.load(bins_ptr + d) 

652 steps = nbins + 1 

653 half = steps // 2 

654 l_edge = left.to(ACC_DTYPE) 

655 r_edge = right.to(ACC_DTYPE) 

656 step = tl.math.div_rn(r_edge - l_edge, nbins.to(ACC_DTYPE)) 

657 for base in range(0, MAX_EDGES, BLOCK_E): 

658 idx = base + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_E) 

659 m = idx < MAX_EDGES 

660 fi = idx.to(ACC_DTYPE) 

661 rev = (steps - 1 - idx).to(ACC_DTYPE) 

662 val = tl.where(idx < half, step * fi + l_edge, r_edge - step * rev) 

663 # Padding lanes hold +inf so the binning search never selects 

664 # them. 

665 val = tl.where(idx <= nbins, val, float("inf")) 

666 tl.store(edges_ptr + d * MAX_EDGES + idx, val, mask=m) 

667 

668 

669@libentry() 

670@triton.jit 

671def histogramdd_bin_geometry_kernel( 

672 left_ptr, # (N,) left edges 

673 right_ptr, # (N,) right edges 

674 bins_ptr, # (N,) bins per dimension 

675 width_ptr, # (N,) out: right - left 

676 bin_width_ptr, # (N,) out: width / bins (width == 0 -> 1) 

677 N, 

678 ACC_DTYPE: tl.constexpr, 

679 BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr, 

680): 

681 """Derive per-dimension widths and bin widths on the device. 

682 

683 Keeps this off the host, so no ``.item()`` per dimension is needed to 

684 build the kernel arguments. 

685 """ 

686 cols = ext.program_id(0) * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N) 

687 mask = cols < N 

688 left = tl.load(left_ptr + cols, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(ACC_DTYPE) 

689 right = tl.load(right_ptr + cols, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(ACC_DTYPE) 

690 nbins = tl.load(bins_ptr + cols, mask=mask, other=1).to(ACC_DTYPE) 

691 

692 width = right - left 

693 # Guard a zero width so the division in the density scale stays finite; 

694 # such points only match the ``coord == right`` branch in the binning 

695 # anyway. 

696 safe = tl.where(width == 0, 1.0, width) 

697 tl.store(width_ptr + cols, width, mask=mask) 

698 tl.store(bin_width_ptr + cols, safe / nbins, mask=mask) 

699 

700 

701@libentry() 

702@triton.jit 

703def histogramdd_total_scale_kernel( 

704 hist_ptr, # (num_bins,) counts 

705 log_width_ptr, # () log of the absolute bin volume 

706 sign_ptr, # () sign of the bin volume 

707 scale_ptr, # () out: 1 / (total_count * bin_volume) 

708 num_bins, 

709 ACC_DTYPE: tl.constexpr, 

710 BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr, 

711): 

712 """Sum the histogram and turn it into the density scale, entirely on device. 

713 

714 Replaces the host ``hist_acc.sum().item()``. The bin volume is accumulated 

715 in the log domain and re-exponentiated so a many-dimensional product 

716 cannot overflow before the division. The division is left unguarded on 

717 purpose: ATen divides straight through, so a zero total yields inf/nan 

718 and those must propagate (see the density notes in the host function). 

719 """ 

720 total = tl.zeros((), dtype=ACC_DTYPE) 

721 for base in range(0, num_bins, BLOCK_SIZE): 

722 offs = base + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

723 m = offs < num_bins 

724 total += tl.sum(tl.load(hist_ptr + offs, mask=m, other=0.0).to(ACC_DTYPE)) 

725 

726 # The bin volume arrives already reduced (a signed magnitude in the log 

727 # domain) because it depends only on the bins list and the edges, not on 

728 # the data. 

729 log_vol = tl.load(log_width_ptr).to(ACC_DTYPE) 

730 sign = tl.load(sign_ptr).to(ACC_DTYPE) 

731 bin_volume = sign * tl.exp(log_vol) 

732 tl.store(scale_ptr, 1.0 / (total * bin_volume)) 

733 

734 

735@libentry() 

736@triton.jit 

737def histogramdd_log_volume_kernel( 

738 width_ptr, # (N,) per-dimension width 

739 bins_ptr, # (N,) per-dimension bin count 

740 log_width_ptr, # () out: sum of log|width / bins| 

741 sign_ptr, # () out: product of the signs 

742 N, 

743 ACC_DTYPE: tl.constexpr, 

744 BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr, 

745): 

746 """Reduce the per-dimension bin widths into a signed log bin volume. 

747 

748 Accumulating ``log|width / bins|`` and tracking the sign separately keeps 

749 a high-dimensional product from overflowing or underflowing before the 

750 division in ``histogramdd_total_scale_kernel``. 

751 """ 

752 offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N) 

753 m = offs < N 

754 width = tl.load(width_ptr + offs, mask=m, other=1.0).to(ACC_DTYPE) 

755 nbins = tl.load(bins_ptr + offs, mask=m, other=1).to(ACC_DTYPE) 

756 per_dim = width / nbins 

757 # Masked lanes contribute log(1) == 0 to the sum and +1 to the sign 

758 # product. 

759 mag = tl.where(m, tl.abs(per_dim), 1.0) 

760 tl.store(log_width_ptr, tl.sum(tl.log(mag), axis=0)) 

761 negatives = tl.sum(tl.where(m & (per_dim < 0), 1, 0), axis=0) 

762 tl.store(sign_ptr, tl.where(negatives % 2 == 0, 1.0, -1.0).to(ACC_DTYPE)) 

763 

764 

765def _format_bound(value): 

766 """Format a range bound the way ATen's range messages do. 

767 

768 ATen uses the default C++ stream formatting, which is ``%g`` (six 

769 significant digits, scientific notation outside a fixed exponent 

770 window), so ``0.123456789`` prints as ``0.123457`` and ``1e7`` as 

771 ``1e+07``. 

772 """ 

773 return "%g" % value 

774 

775 

776def _validate_and_widen_range(range_, N): 

777 """Validate an explicit range like ATen, widening zero-width dimensions. 

778 

779 Returns the post-widening float list. ATen validates every dimension's 

780 bounds in this order: first that they are finite, then that min <= max; 

781 an explicit non-finite bound is rejected too, not just a non-finite 

782 auto-range. ATen then widens a zero-width dimension before building the 

783 edges ("Expand empty range to match numpy behavior and avoid division by 

784 0 in normalization"), so an explicit [1.0, 1.0] behaves exactly like the 

785 degenerate *auto*-range case: the edges become linspace(l - .5, r + .5, 

786 bins + 1) and a point at 1.0 lands in bin bins // 2 rather than being 

787 folded into the last bin. 

788 """ 

789 rng = [float(v) for v in range_] 

790 if len(rng) != 2 * N: 

791 raise RuntimeError( 

792 f"torch.histogramdd: for a {N}-dimensional histogram range should " 

793 f"have {2 * N} elements, but got {len(rng)}" 

794 ) 

795 for d in range(N): 

796 lo, hi = rng[2 * d], rng[2 * d + 1] 

797 if not (math.isfinite(lo) and math.isfinite(hi)): 

798 raise RuntimeError( 

799 f"torch.histogramdd: dimension {d}'s range " 

800 f"[{_format_bound(lo)}, {_format_bound(hi)}] is not finite" 

801 ) 

802 if lo > hi: 

803 raise RuntimeError( 

804 f"torch.histogramdd: min should not exceed max, but got " 

805 f"min {_format_bound(lo)} max {_format_bound(hi)} for " 

806 f"dimension {d}" 

807 ) 

808 for d in range(N): 

809 if rng[2 * d] == rng[2 * d + 1]: 

810 rng[2 * d] -= 0.5 

811 rng[2 * d + 1] += 0.5 

812 return rng 

813 

814 

815def _get_bins_meta(device, bins_list): 

816 """Per-(device, bins) metadata: strides, bins tensor, dummy weight slot. 

817 

818 Derived purely from the bins list (host data), so the tensors are built 

819 once and cached; the ~30 us pageable H2D of a ``torch.tensor`` call was 

820 paid four times per call before this cache existed. 

821 """ 

822 key = (device, tuple(bins_list)) 

823 ent = _BINS_META_CACHE.get(key) 

824 if ent is None: 

825 N = len(bins_list) 

826 strides_host = [1] * N 

827 for d in _builtins.range(N - 2, -1, -1): 

828 strides_host[d] = strides_host[d + 1] * bins_list[d + 1] 

829 ent = _meta_cache_put( 

830 _BINS_META_CACHE, 

831 key, 

832 { 

833 "strides": torch.tensor(strides_host, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), 

834 "bins": torch.tensor(bins_list, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), 

835 # Triton needs a valid pointer slot even when HAS_WEIGHT 

836 # is False; the kernel never loads from it. 

837 "wdummy": torch.empty(1, dtype=torch.float32, device=device), 

838 }, 

839 ) 

840 return ent 

841 

842 

843def _get_range_meta(device, bins_list, rng, bins_meta): 

844 """Per-(device, bins, range) metadata: bounds, edges, density geometry. 

845 

846 The edges are produced by the very same ``histogramdd_edges_kernel`` the 

847 per-call path used to launch, so the cached values are bit-identical to 

848 what a fresh call would build -- only the launch (and its ~30 us host 

849 cost) is skipped. The density geometry (widths / bin widths) is a pure 

850 function of the bounds and bins, so it is cached alongside. 

851 """ 

852 key = (device, tuple(bins_list), tuple(rng)) 

853 ent = _RANGE_META_CACHE.get(key) 

854 if ent is None: 

855 N = len(bins_list) 

856 max_edges = max(bins_list) + 1 

857 lefts = torch.tensor(rng[0::2], dtype=torch.float32, device=device) 

858 rights = torch.tensor(rng[1::2], dtype=torch.float32, device=device) 

859 edges = torch.empty(N, max_edges, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) 

860 widths = torch.empty(N, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) 

861 bin_widths = torch.empty(N, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) 

862 bins_t = bins_meta["bins"] 

863 BLOCK_N = triton.next_power_of_2(N) 

864 with torch_device_fn.device(device): 

865 histogramdd_edges_kernel[(N,)]( 

866 lefts, 

867 rights, 

868 bins_t, 

869 edges, 

870 N, 

871 max_edges, 

872 ACC_DTYPE=tl.float32, 

873 BLOCK_E=min(1024, triton.next_power_of_2(max_edges)), 

874 ) 

875 histogramdd_bin_geometry_kernel[(triton.cdiv(N, BLOCK_N),)]( 

876 lefts, 

877 rights, 

878 bins_t, 

879 widths, 

880 bin_widths, 

881 N, 

882 ACC_DTYPE=tl.float32, 

883 BLOCK_N=BLOCK_N, 

884 ) 

885 ent = _meta_cache_put( 

886 _RANGE_META_CACHE, 

887 key, 

888 { 

889 "lefts": lefts, 

890 "rights": rights, 

891 "edges": edges, 

892 "max_edges": max_edges, 

893 "widths": widths, 

894 "bin_widths": bin_widths, 

895 }, 

896 ) 

897 return ent 

898 

899 

900def _get_partials(device, rows, cols): 

901 """Cached int32 partial-count buffer of shape (rows, cols). 

902 

903 Every element of every row is unconditionally stored by the counting 

904 kernels (the padding column included), so the buffer never needs 

905 zero-initialisation and a cached ``torch.empty`` is safe to reuse.""" 

906 key = (device, rows, cols) 

907 ent = _PARTIALS_CACHE.get(key) 

908 if ent is None: 

909 ent = _meta_cache_put( 

910 _PARTIALS_CACHE, 

911 key, 

912 torch.empty(rows * cols, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), 

913 ) 

914 return ent 

915 

916 

917def _auto_range(inp, N): 

918 """Derive the per-dimension range from the data, on the device. 

919 

920 Matches torch.histogramdd: a dimension whose min equals max is expanded 

921 to (min - 0.5, max + 0.5). The range endpoints are float32 because 

922 GCU400 has no FP64 vector path (torch_gcu downgrades float64 tensors to 

923 float32 storage and fp64 kernels crash the compiler). 

924 """ 

925 lefts = torch.empty(N, dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device) 

926 rights = torch.empty(N, dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device) 

927 M = inp.shape[0] 

928 if M == 0: 

929 # No data to reduce over; ATen's empty-input range collapses to (0, 1) 

930 # per dimension after the degenerate-range expansion of (inf, -inf) is 

931 # skipped. 

932 lefts.fill_(0.0) 

933 rights.fill_(1.0) 

934 return lefts, rights, None 

935 

936 BLOCK_N = triton.next_power_of_2(N) 

937 grid = (triton.cdiv(N, BLOCK_N),) 

938 # Sentinel-initialised to N: the kernel only lowers it, so a finite input 

939 # leaves it at N and the check below reads one scalar instead of running 

940 # ``isfinite``/``nonzero`` over the whole range tensor on the host. 

941 nonfinite_dim = torch.full((), N, dtype=torch.int32, device=inp.device) 

942 with torch_device_fn.device(inp.device): 

943 histogramdd_col_range_kernel[grid]( 

944 inp, 

945 lefts, 

946 rights, 

947 nonfinite_dim, 

948 M, 

949 N, 

950 ACC_DTYPE=tl.float32, 

951 BLOCK_M=128, 

952 BLOCK_N=BLOCK_N, 

953 SENTINEL=N, 

954 ) 

955 return lefts, rights, nonfinite_dim 

956 

957 

958def _check_finite_auto_range(lefts, rights, nonfinite_dim, N): 

959 """Reject a non-finite auto-range, with ATen's message. 

960 

961 The bound is printed for the offending dimension, so that dimension has 

962 to be known before raising; ``histogramdd_col_range_kernel`` reports it 

963 in ``nonfinite_dim`` (sentinel ``N`` meaning "all finite") so this stays 

964 a single scalar read. ``%g`` reproduces ATen's formatting. 

965 """ 

966 dim = int(nonfinite_dim.item()) 

967 if dim >= N: 

968 return 

969 raise RuntimeError( 

970 f"torch.histogramdd: dimension {dim}'s range " 

971 f"[{_format_bound(lefts[dim].item())}, {_format_bound(rights[dim].item())}] " 

972 "is not finite" 

973 ) 

974 

975 

976def _histogramdd_from_bin_cts_impl( 

977 self, bins, *, range=None, weight=None, density=False, out=None 

978): 

979 """Shared implementation for the base and ``.out`` ATen variants.""" 

980 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME _HISTOGRAMDD_FROM_BIN_CTS") 

981 

982 if self.ndim < 2: 

983 raise RuntimeError( 

984 "torch.histogramdd: input tensor should have at least 2 dimensions" 

985 ) 

986 if self.shape[-1] != len(bins): 

987 raise RuntimeError( 

988 "histogramdd: The size of bins must be equal to the innermost " 

989 "dimension of the input." 

990 ) 

991 

992 # torch._histogramdd_from_bin_cts is only implemented for floating types. 

993 if not self.is_floating_point(): 

994 raise NotImplementedError('"histogramdd" not implemented for this dtype') 

995 

996 if weight is not None and weight.dtype != self.dtype: 

997 raise RuntimeError( 

998 "torch.histogramdd: if weight tensor is provided, input tensor and " 

999 "weight tensor should have the same dtype, but got " 

1000 f"input({self.dtype}), and weight({weight.dtype})" 

1001 ) 

1002 

1003 N = self.shape[-1] 

1004 bins_list = [int(b) for b in bins] 

1005 out_shape = tuple(bins_list) 

1006 

1007 out_dtype = self.dtype 

1008 

1009 if self.dtype == torch.float64: 

1010 # gcu400 has no fp64 arithmetic. Bin placement compares the coordinate 

1011 # against the edges exactly, so a coordinate one ulp away from an edge 

1012 # cannot be classified in fp32 (and the fp64 kernels do not compile). 

1013 # Delegate double precision to the native CPU implementation and copy 

1014 # the result back. 

1015 cpu = torch.ops.aten._histogramdd_from_bin_cts( 

1016 self.cpu(), 

1017 bins_list, 

1018 range=None if range is None else [float(v) for v in range], 

1019 weight=None if weight is None else weight.cpu(), 

1020 density=density, 

1021 ) 

1022 if out is None: 

1023 return cpu.to(self.device) 

1024 if out.dtype != out_dtype: 

1025 raise RuntimeError( 

1026 f"Expected out tensor to have dtype {out_dtype}, but got " 

1027 f"{out.dtype} instead" 

1028 ) 

1029 if tuple(out.shape) != tuple(cpu.shape): 

1030 out.resize_(cpu.shape) 

1031 out.copy_(cpu) 

1032 return out 

1033 

1034 # GCU400 has no FP64 vector path: torch_gcu downgrades float64 tensors to 

1035 # float32 storage, and fp64 Triton kernels crash the GCU compiler. 

1036 # Normalise the compute input to real float32 while out keeps the 

1037 # caller's dtype. 

1038 compute_input = self.to(torch.float32) if out_dtype != torch.float32 else self 

1039 

1040 # Flatten all leading dims to (M, N) and make contiguous. 

1041 inp = compute_input.reshape(-1, N).contiguous() 

1042 M = inp.shape[0] 

1043 

1044 # Allocate / validate the output buffer. ATen resizes a mis-shaped out 

1045 # tensor in place and keeps the caller's object identity, but rejects a 

1046 # dtype mismatch outright, so a wrong dtype must raise rather than be 

1047 # re-bound through .to() (which would leave the caller's buffer 

1048 # untouched). 

1049 if out is not None: 

1050 if out.dtype != out_dtype: 

1051 raise RuntimeError( 

1052 f"Expected out tensor to have dtype {out_dtype}, but got " 

1053 f"{out.dtype} instead" 

1054 ) 

1055 if out.device != self.device: 

1056 raise RuntimeError( 

1057 f"Expected out tensor to have device {self.device}, but got " 

1058 f"{out.device} instead" 

1059 ) 

1060 if tuple(out.shape) != out_shape: 

1061 out.resize_(out_shape) 

1062 else: 

1063 out = torch.empty(out_shape, dtype=out_dtype, device=self.device) 

1064 

1065 if out.numel() == 0: 

1066 # No bins to fill; zero the output and return. 

1067 out.zero_() 

1068 return out 

1069 

1070 bins_meta = _get_bins_meta(inp.device, bins_list) 

1071 strides = bins_meta["strides"] 

1072 bins_t = bins_meta["bins"] 

1073 

1074 if range is not None: 

1075 rng = _validate_and_widen_range(range, N) 

1076 range_meta = _get_range_meta(inp.device, bins_list, rng, bins_meta) 

1077 lefts = range_meta["lefts"] 

1078 rights = range_meta["rights"] 

1079 edges = range_meta["edges"] 

1080 max_edges = range_meta["max_edges"] 

1081 widths = range_meta["widths"] 

1082 bin_widths = range_meta["bin_widths"] 

1083 else: 

1084 # Auto range: the bounds depend on the data, so nothing but the bins 

1085 # metadata can be reused across calls. 

1086 lefts, rights, nonfinite_dim = _auto_range(inp, N) 

1087 if nonfinite_dim is not None: 

1088 _check_finite_auto_range(lefts, rights, nonfinite_dim, N) 

1089 max_edges = max(bins_list) + 1 

1090 edges = torch.empty(N, max_edges, dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device) 

1091 widths = torch.empty(N, dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device) 

1092 bin_widths = torch.empty(N, dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device) 

1093 BLOCK_N = triton.next_power_of_2(N) 

1094 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

1095 histogramdd_edges_kernel[(N,)]( 

1096 lefts, 

1097 rights, 

1098 bins_t, 

1099 edges, 

1100 N, 

1101 max_edges, 

1102 ACC_DTYPE=tl.float32, 

1103 BLOCK_E=min(1024, triton.next_power_of_2(max_edges)), 

1104 ) 

1105 histogramdd_bin_geometry_kernel[(triton.cdiv(N, BLOCK_N),)]( 

1106 lefts, 

1107 rights, 

1108 bins_t, 

1109 widths, 

1110 bin_widths, 

1111 N, 

1112 ACC_DTYPE=tl.float32, 

1113 BLOCK_N=BLOCK_N, 

1114 ) 

1115 

1116 num_bins = 1 

1117 for b in bins_list: 

1118 num_bins *= b 

1119 steps_const = max(1, (max_edges - 1).bit_length()) 

1120 

1121 # Counts land in a real float32 buffer. A contiguous float32 out can 

1122 # serve as that buffer directly (the reduce kernels overwrite every 

1123 # bin, so no zero-fill is needed); other dtypes and non-contiguous outs 

1124 # need a temporary plus one copy to keep the .out contract intact. 

1125 hist_is_out = not density and out.dtype == torch.float32 and out.is_contiguous() 

1126 if hist_is_out: 

1127 hist_target = out.view(num_bins) 

1128 else: 

1129 hist_target = torch.empty(num_bins, dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device) 

1130 

1131 has_weight = weight is not None 

1132 if has_weight: 

1133 weight = weight.reshape(-1).contiguous() 

1134 if weight.dtype != torch.float32: 

1135 weight = weight.to(torch.float32) 

1136 if weight.numel() != M: 

1137 raise RuntimeError( 

1138 "_histogramdd_from_bin_cts: weight must have the same number " 

1139 "of rows as the input" 

1140 ) 

1141 

1142 if M == 0: 

1143 # No points: the histogram is all zeros, whatever the dispatch 

1144 # path would have been. 

1145 hist_target.zero_() 

1146 else: 

1147 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

1148 if has_weight: 

1149 # Weighted calls scatter-add one contribution per point; 

1150 # per-program private slab rows keep the same-address 

1151 # atomic collision depth bounded by the tile size instead 

1152 # of the grid size. 

1153 grid_n = triton.cdiv(M, _SLAB_BLOCK) 

1154 if grid_n * num_bins * 4 <= _MAX_SLAB_BYTES: 

1155 slab = torch.zeros( 

1156 grid_n * num_bins, dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device 

1157 ) 

1158 histogramdd_weighted_slab_kernel[(grid_n,)]( 

1159 inp, 

1160 weight, 

1161 slab, 

1162 M, 

1163 N, 

1164 lefts, 

1165 rights, 

1166 edges, 

1167 strides, 

1168 bins_t, 

1169 max_edges, 

1170 MAX_EDGE_STEPS=steps_const, 

1171 N_CONST=N, 

1172 BLOCK_SIZE=_SLAB_BLOCK, 

1173 NUM_BINS=num_bins, 

1174 ) 

1175 histogramdd_reduce_slab_kernel[(triton.cdiv(num_bins, 1024),)]( 

1176 slab, 

1177 hist_target, 

1178 grid_n, 

1179 NUM_BINS=num_bins, 

1180 BLOCK_B=1024, 

1181 ) 

1182 else: 

1183 # Pathological point count x bin width: a private slab 

1184 # would exceed the scratch budget, so pay the shared 

1185 # same-address atomics instead. 

1186 hist_target.zero_() 

1187 histogramdd_direct_kernel[(grid_n,)]( 

1188 inp, 

1189 weight, 

1190 hist_target, 

1191 M, 

1192 N, 

1193 lefts, 

1194 rights, 

1195 edges, 

1196 strides, 

1197 bins_t, 

1198 max_edges, 

1199 MAX_EDGE_STEPS=steps_const, 

1200 N_CONST=N, 

1201 BLOCK_SIZE=_SLAB_BLOCK, 

1202 HAS_WEIGHT=True, 

1203 ) 

1204 elif num_bins <= 512: 

1205 # Narrow bin grid: count with per-program partials (no 

1206 # global atomics at all) and one reduce kernel. 

1207 hist_bins = triton.next_power_of_2(num_bins + 1) 

1208 if hist_bins <= _DOT_PERSISTENT_MAX_BINS: 

1209 # One-hot int8 tl.dot on a persistent grid; a single 

1210 # chunk covers the whole padded bin vector. 

1211 grid_n = min(triton.cdiv(M, _DOT_BLOCK), MAX_CTAS) 

1212 partials = _get_partials(inp.device, grid_n, hist_bins) 

1213 histogramdd_dot_persistent_kernel[(grid_n,)]( 

1214 inp, 

1215 partials, 

1216 M, 

1217 N, 

1218 lefts, 

1219 rights, 

1220 edges, 

1221 strides, 

1222 bins_t, 

1223 max_edges, 

1224 MAX_EDGE_STEPS=steps_const, 

1225 N_CONST=N, 

1226 BLOCK_SIZE=_DOT_BLOCK, 

1227 NUM_BINS=num_bins, 

1228 HIST_BINS=hist_bins, 

1229 NB_CHUNK=max(hist_bins, 16), 

1230 ) 

1231 elif M < _DOT_MAX_POINTS: 

1232 # Wider bin vector but a small point cloud: chunked 

1233 # one-hot dot, one program per tile. 

1234 grid_n = triton.cdiv(M, _DOT_BLOCK) 

1235 partials = _get_partials(inp.device, grid_n, hist_bins) 

1236 histogramdd_dot_kernel[(grid_n,)]( 

1237 inp, 

1238 partials, 

1239 M, 

1240 N, 

1241 lefts, 

1242 rights, 

1243 edges, 

1244 strides, 

1245 bins_t, 

1246 max_edges, 

1247 MAX_EDGE_STEPS=steps_const, 

1248 N_CONST=N, 

1249 BLOCK_SIZE=_DOT_BLOCK, 

1250 NUM_BINS=num_bins, 

1251 HIST_BINS=hist_bins, 

1252 NB_CHUNK=128, 

1253 ) 

1254 else: 

1255 # Large point cloud over a wide bin vector: the per-point 

1256 # one-hot compare cost overtakes the histogram 

1257 # primitive's per-bin cost. 

1258 grid_n = triton.cdiv(M, _HIST_BLOCK) 

1259 partials = _get_partials(inp.device, grid_n, hist_bins) 

1260 histogramdd_hist_partial_kernel[(grid_n,)]( 

1261 inp, 

1262 partials, 

1263 M, 

1264 N, 

1265 lefts, 

1266 rights, 

1267 edges, 

1268 strides, 

1269 bins_t, 

1270 max_edges, 

1271 MAX_EDGE_STEPS=steps_const, 

1272 N_CONST=N, 

1273 BLOCK_SIZE=_HIST_BLOCK, 

1274 HIST_BINS=hist_bins, 

1275 ) 

1276 histogramdd_reduce_i32_kernel[(triton.cdiv(num_bins, 512),)]( 

1277 partials, 

1278 hist_target, 

1279 grid_n, 

1280 HIST_BINS=hist_bins, 

1281 NUM_BINS=num_bins, 

1282 BLOCK_B=512, 

1283 ) 

1284 else: 

1285 # Wide bin grid: per-point atomics into the zeroed 

1286 # accumulator. Per-address collisions stay rare (points 

1287 # spread over many bins), and no per-program aggregation 

1288 # beats the atomic unit's throughput at this width. 

1289 block = 256 if M <= 8192 else 512 

1290 grid_n = triton.cdiv(M, block) 

1291 hist_target.zero_() 

1292 histogramdd_direct_kernel[(grid_n,)]( 

1293 inp, 

1294 bins_meta["wdummy"], 

1295 hist_target, 

1296 M, 

1297 N, 

1298 lefts, 

1299 rights, 

1300 edges, 

1301 strides, 

1302 bins_t, 

1303 max_edges, 

1304 MAX_EDGE_STEPS=steps_const, 

1305 N_CONST=N, 

1306 BLOCK_SIZE=block, 

1307 HAS_WEIGHT=False, 

1308 ) 

1309 

1310 if density: 

1311 # density[i] = count[i] / (total_count * bin_volume), where 

1312 # bin_volume is the volume of a single (equal-width) N-dimensional 

1313 # bin, i.e. the product of the per-dimension bin widths = 

1314 # prod((right - left) / bins). Both reductions run on the device; 

1315 # the scale kernel reads the counts buffer directly. 

1316 log_vol = torch.empty((), dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device) 

1317 vol_sign = torch.empty((), dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device) 

1318 scale_t = torch.empty((), dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device) 

1319 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

1320 histogramdd_log_volume_kernel[(1,)]( 

1321 widths, 

1322 bins_t, 

1323 log_vol, 

1324 vol_sign, 

1325 N, 

1326 ACC_DTYPE=tl.float32, 

1327 BLOCK_N=triton.next_power_of_2(N), 

1328 ) 

1329 # The division is deliberately unguarded: ATen divides by the 

1330 # total count directly, so an empty or fully out-of-range input 

1331 # yields NaN and weights that cancel to zero yield +-inf. Forcing 

1332 # the scale to zero here would silently diverge from that. 

1333 histogramdd_total_scale_kernel[(1,)]( 

1334 hist_target, 

1335 log_vol, 

1336 vol_sign, 

1337 scale_t, 

1338 num_bins, 

1339 ACC_DTYPE=tl.float32, 

1340 BLOCK_SIZE=1024, 

1341 ) 

1342 # Density values are produced in a flat fp32 buffer and copied into 

1343 # the caller's out at the end, so fp16 / non-contiguous outs stay 

1344 # correct. 

1345 out_flat = torch.empty(num_bins, dtype=torch.float32, device=inp.device) 

1346 if num_bins > 0: 

1347 BLOCK = 1024 

1348 with torch_device_fn.device(self.device): 

1349 histogramdd_density_kernel[(triton.cdiv(num_bins, BLOCK),)]( 

1350 hist_target, 

1351 out_flat, 

1352 scale_t, 

1353 num_bins, 

1354 ACC_DTYPE=tl.float32, 

1355 BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK, 

1356 ) 

1357 out.copy_(out_flat.view(out_shape)) 

1358 elif not hist_is_out: 

1359 out.copy_(hist_target.view(out_shape)) 

1360 

1361 return out 

1362

1365 """aten::_histogramdd_from_bin_cts(Tensor self, int[] bins, *, float[]? range=None, 

1366 Tensor? weight=None, bool density=False) -> Tensor 

1367 """ 

1368 return _histogramdd_from_bin_cts_impl( 

1369 self, bins, range=range, weight=weight, density=density, out=None 

1370 ) 

1371 

1372

1375): 

1376 """aten::_histogramdd_from_bin_cts.out(Tensor self, int[] bins, *, float[]? range=None,

1378 """

1380 self, bins, range=range, weight=weight, density=density, out=out
